One-cop-moves escape certificate on a planar graph

The finite undirected graph has a hub H and 16777216 spokes.  A spoke is identified
by an integer label x with 0 <= x < 16777216.  For every label x it has vertices
(x,1),...,(x,4194304); H is adjacent to (x,1), consecutive depths on one spoke
are adjacent, and the boundary vertices (x,4194304) form one cycle in the order
defined below.  Thus the graph is a planar subdivided wheel.

Boundary order.  Number cyclic positions i=0,...,16777215.  All bit operations
use exactly 24 low bits, numbered from least-significant bit 0.  A left rotation
by r moves bit j to bit (j+r) mod 24.  Let gray(z)=z XOR floor(z/2).  To obtain
the spoke label B(i), start with gray((11108267 +
-1*i) mod 16777216); move source bit j to output bit p[j]
for
  p = [1, 4, 19, 14, 13, 6, 8, 20, 22, 21, 2, 3, 7, 15, 23, 11, 17, 18, 5, 16, 10, 0, 12, 9];
XOR the result with 441911; then apply these [left-rotation, XOR-mask]
pairs from left to right:
  twists = [[21,4181310],[11,15983232],[18,15121532]].
Here left-rotation is cyclic on 24 bits.  The boundary cycle has edges between
(B(i),4194304) and (B((i+1) mod 16777216),4194304).

Game configuration.  The robber is at H and moves first.  In every round the
robber traverses one edge and afterward exactly one of the three cops traverses
one edge.  A cop catches the robber by ever occupying her vertex.  The cops are
on the following spokes; depth is graph distance from H:
  cop 1: (label=8419823, depth=3073700), cop 2: (label=10730094, depth=2701316), cop 3: (label=9307451, depth=2613590)

Your witness must select a canonical spoke path from H through
(x,1),(x,2),...,(x,4194304).  It is valid exactly when, for each of the three cops,
the cop's initial shortest-path distance to endpoint (x,4194304) is strictly greater
than 4194304.  This exact inequality certifies that the robber reaches the endpoint
without capture even if that cop were allowed to move after every robber step.
There is exactly one valid label.  Labels are decimal integers; indexing is
0-based; no other path kind or extra field is allowed.
